1. Given two tables as follows.
• CREATE TABLE t1(A INT NOT NULL, B INT NOT NULL)
• CREATE TABLE t2(A INT NOT NULL, C INT NOT NULL)
The number of tuples in t1 is Nr ≥ 1 and in t2 is Ns ≥ 1. What is the minimum / minimum number of
tuples in
• SELECT * FROM t1 CROSS JOIN t2
• SELECT * FROM t1 INNER JOIN t2
• SELECT * FROM t1 JOIN t2
• SELECT * FROM t1 NATURAL JOIN t2
• SELECT * FROM t1 NATURAL LEFT OUTER JOIN t2;
• SELECT * FROM t1 NATURAL RIGHT OUTER JOIN t2;
Maximum Minimum
CROSS JOIN Nr × Ns Nr × Ns
INNER JOIN Nr × Ns Nr × Ns
JOIN Nr × Ns Nr × Ns
NATURAL JOIN Nr × Ns 0
NATURAL LEFT OUTER JOIN Nr × Ns Nr
NATURAL RIGHT OUTER JOIN Nr × Ns Ns
2. Given two tables as follows.
• CREATE TABLE t1(A INT PRIMARY KEY, B INT NOT NULL)
• CREATE TABLE t2(A INT PRIMARY KEY, C INT NOT NULL)
The number of tuples in t1 is Nr ≥ 1 and in t2 is Ns ≥ 1. What is the maximum / minimum number of
tuples in
• SELECT * FROM t1 CROSS JOIN t2
• SELECT * FROM t1 INNER JOIN t2
• SELECT * FROM t1 JOIN t2
• SELECT * FROM t1 NATURAL JOIN t2
• SELECT * FROM t1 NATURAL LEFT OUTER JOIN t2;
• SELECT * FROM t1 NATURAL RIGHT OUTER JOIN t2;
Maximum Minimum
CROSS JOIN Nr × Ns Nr × Ns
INNER JOIN Nr × Ns Nr × Ns
JOIN Nr × Ns Nr × Ns
NATURAL JOIN min (Nr, Ns) 0
NATURAL LEFT OUTER JOIN Nr Nr
NATURAL RIGHT OUTER JOIN Ns Ns
